turns.q: Why is the sky blue?
turns.reply: The sky is blue because it is made up of tiny, blue particles called atoms. When light enters the atmosphere, it interacts with the atoms in the air, causing them to scatter and scatter in all directions. The blue light is then absorbed by the molecules in the air, creating a blue color. The sun, in turn, emits this blue light, which is then reflected back into space, creating a beautiful blue sky.
